branches.note: Trailers weighing 2,000 lb or more are required to be titled in Florida per F.S. §319.14. HSMV 82040 is the title application.
Trailers under 2,000 lb cannot be titled in Florida (per HSMV TL-10) and are registration-only. No title application needed.
Homemade trailers — bring all parts receipts. 6% sales tax is calculated on the total cost of materials.

Homemade trailers ≥2,000 lb need a state-assigned VIN. Compliance Examiner inspects the trailer in-office, assigns the VIN, and completes HSMV 82042. HSMV 84490 (Statement of Builder) is sometimes also required at the examiner's discretion — bring it filled out to avoid a return trip.

No parts receipts? You can still register the same day: declare the value of the trailer and pay 6% sales tax on that declared value. (Bringing receipts is preferred so tax is figured on actual material cost, but they are not required.) [Confirmed by TCSLC staff — policy-questions REG-1, 2026-07.]

Private purchase of a sub-2,000 lb trailer — the bill of sale from the prior owner is the proof of ownership (no title exists). Bring the bill of sale showing trailer description, purchase price, and date.
Private purchase of a ≥2,000 lb trailer — the seller signs over the existing FL title. VIN verification (HSMV 82042) is required because the trailer is changing ownership.
Dealer purchase — dealer collects FL sales tax at point of sale. Bring the dealer bill of sale showing the tax breakdown. For ≥2,000 lb the dealer also provides MCO or signed-over title.
Dealer-purchased ≥2,000 lb trailers come with a Manufacturer Certificate of Origin (new) or signed-over title (used dealer inventory). The dealer hands this to the customer at sale.

Inherited trailer — bring the deceased prior owner's death certificate plus their existing trailer title (if ≥2,000 lb) signed via probate process. For sub-2,000 lb trailers, the death certificate establishes chain of ownership; no title transfer is needed.

Inherited ≥2,000 lb trailer — the prior owner's FL title must be transferred. Probate court documents or a surviving-spouse affidavit may substitute for a signed-over title. Office may require additional paperwork at the examiner's discretion.
Out-of-state transfer of a ≥2,000 lb trailer — the OOS title is surrendered to FL and a new FL title is issued. VIN verification (HSMV 82042) is required.
Out-of-state transfer of a sub-2,000 lb trailer — bring the OOS registration as proof of prior ownership. No title is required (FL doesn't title trailers <2,000 lb).
